label: Amazon Web Services

corePack.why: If CloudTrail is not delivered, you have no account-level audit trail.
corePack.whyNow: Delivery failures are how attackers and misconfig hide.

corePack.why: StopLogging is an integrity attack on the same audit trail.
corePack.whyNow: Treat CloudTrail disablement as an incident, not a config footnote.

corePack.why: GuardDuty is AWS-native threat findings already scored for you.
corePack.whyNow: Ingest findings before you invent custom detections.

corePack.why: Config drift is the control-plane change you did not intend.
corePack.whyNow: Compliance and availability both fail when rules go NON_COMPLIANT.

corePack.why: Root account usage is never routine in a well-run account.
corePack.whyNow: Root is the break-glass identity; every use is an audit event.

corePack.why: IAM policy changes alter who can do what in the account.
corePack.whyNow: Privilege changes should be reviewed the same day they land.

corePack.why: Severity analysis turns GuardDuty volume into a queue.
corePack.whyNow: High/critical findings need owners, not a dashboard of counts.

valueHypothesis: AWS monitoring should start with CloudTrail integrity and delivery, GuardDuty, Config drift, and IAM/root—the controls AWS itself treats as the account security baseline—not incidental mentions of AWS in other products.
rationale: AWS security guidance and Splunk Lantern cloud content lead with CloudTrail health, GuardDuty, Config, and IAM/root monitoring as the first account-level detections.
